newsitem.title: USA: Continental Air buys 10 leased aircraft.
newsitem.headline: Continental Air buys 10 leased aircraft.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc, the fifth largest U.S. airline, said it acquired 10 aircraft it previously leased.

The deal is expected to decrease aircraft ownership costs by about $3 million a year over the next three years compared with the costs the company would have incurred if it continued to lease the planes, the Houston-based carrier said.

Aircraft maintenance expenses in the second quarter of 1997 will be reduced by about $16 million due to the release of reserves that are no longer required as a result of the transaction, Continental said.

The debt financing for the acquisitions of the six Boeing Co 737-300 aircraft and the four McDonnell Douglas Corp MD-82 planes was funded by the private placement of $155 million of pass-through certificates, the company said.
